question: What is the primary purpose of disease surveillance in public health?

options.A: The enforcement of hospital financial budgets and operational policies
options.B: The immediate medical treatment of individual patients in rural clinics
options.C: The systematic collection and analysis of health data to guide public health practice
options.D: The routine administration of vaccines to newborn infants

explanation: Surveillance focuses on gathering and interpreting data to plan and evaluate public health interventions rather than individual treatment. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h1)

question: Why is local clinical observation considered the foundation of national disease surveillance?

options.A: Clinical observations replace the need for laboratory confirmation of diseases
options.B: Local observations feed data upward to national agencies for early epidemic detection
options.C: Local clinics have more funding than international health organizations
options.D: Bedside nurses are solely responsible for writing national health legislation

explanation: Individual clinical observations at the facility level serve as the vital first alert for larger regional or national outbreaks. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h1)

question: What justifies the mandatory reporting of infectious diseases over individual privacy rights?

options.A: The urgent need to protect public safety and prevent widespread community outbreaks
options.B: The desire of pharmaceutical companies to track drug sales and usage
options.C: The need to generate revenue through government health inspection fines
options.D: The requirement to update hospital personnel files on a monthly basis

explanation: Public health laws prioritize community safety and epidemic prevention above individual confidentiality when dealing with dangerous communicable threats. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h2)

question: Which group of professionals holds the statutory obligation to report notifiable diseases in a clinical setting?

options.B: Hospital accountants and financial auditors only
options.D: All attending healthcare providers involved in patient care

explanation: Healthcare providers on the front lines, including nurses and doctors, bear the legal responsibility to report suspected notifiable conditions. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h2)

question: Which timeframe is generally required for reporting Category 1 epidemic-prone diseases?

options.B: At the end of every calendar year

explanation: Category 1 conditions carry high epidemic risks and demand immediate notification, usually within 24 hours, to trigger rapid containment. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h3)

question: A patient presents to a primary health clinic with acute watery diarrhea and severe dehydration during the rainy season, strongly suspected of having cholera. How should this case be classified for notification?
explanation: Cholera is a highly contagious, severe diarrheal illness classified as a Category 1 emergency requiring urgent notification. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h3)

question: Why are nurses considered the frontline of infectious disease surveillance?

options.A: They hold exclusive authority to declare national states of emergency
options.B: They conduct initial patient assessments and spend the most direct time observing clinical signs
options.C: They perform all mandatory molecular laboratory tests independently
options.D: They manage the international transport logistics for vaccines

explanation: Because nurses perform initial triage and ongoing bedside care, they are strategically positioned to spot unusual symptoms and epidemiological links first. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h4)

question: Which action is a primary responsibility of the nurse upon suspecting a highly infectious notifiable disease?

options.A: Discharging the patient immediately to avoid hospital contamination
options.B: Initiating preliminary notification and implementing isolation precautions
options.C: Destroying all clinical charts associated with the patient
options.D: Waiting for national ministers to visit before taking any action

explanation: Prompt isolation and notification are critical nursing actions to stop further pathogen transmission while awaiting formal investigation. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h4)

question: What is the title of the designated officer responsible for coordinating disease surveillance at the local government level in Nigeria?

options.A: Chief Medical Director of Public Works

explanation: The DSNO (Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer) is the specific official tasked with managing disease reports at the local government level. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h5)

question: What is the purpose of following a hierarchical reporting channel from facility to national level?

options.A: To increase paperwork burdens without adding any public health value
options.B: To deliberately delay information sharing until a disease outbreak has naturally ended
options.C: To ensure data verification, coordination, and appropriate resource mobilization at every tier
options.D: To prevent local health workers from ever communicating with federal agencies

explanation: Stepped reporting allows local validation and structured resource allocation as an outbreak moves from facility to national awareness. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h5)

question: What is the primary objective of contact tracing during an infectious disease outbreak?

options.A: To interview hospital administrators about facility cleaning contracts
options.B: To audit the medical insurance status of hospitalized individuals
options.C: To identify and monitor individuals exposed to an infected patient during their incubation period
options.D: To collect financial donations from family members of affected patients

explanation: Contact tracing tracks down exposed persons to monitor for early symptoms and prevent further silent community transmission. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h6)

question: Why do epidemiologists plot an epidemic curve (epi-curve) during an outbreak investigation?

options.A: To visualize the timeline of cases and determine the likely pattern of transmission
options.B: To predict exact weather conditions for the upcoming planting season
options.C: To calculate the annual salary increments for hospital nursing staff
options.D: To determine the architectural layout required for new ward buildings

explanation: An epidemic curve helps investigators see whether an outbreak stems from a single common source or spreads through person-to-person contact. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h6)

question: Which phase of personal protective equipment management is associated with a high risk of accidental contamination for healthcare workers?

options.A: Selecting equipment color schemes for hospital departments
options.C: Purchasing equipment from medical supply vendors
options.D: Storing unused gowns in clean administrative cupboards

explanation: Careless removal or doffing of PPE frequently results in infectious material transferring to the skin or scrubs of healthcare workers. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h7)

question: What is the primary difference between standard precautions and transmission-based precautions?

options.A: Standard precautions are optional guidelines, whereas transmission-based precautions carry criminal penalties
options.B: Standard precautions apply to all patient care universally, whereas transmission-based precautions target specific known or suspected pathogens
options.C: Standard precautions require full biohazard suits, while transmission-based ones require only surgical masks
options.D: Standard precautions are only used in intensive care units, while transmission-based ones are for outpatient clinics

explanation: Standard precautions form the baseline for every patient encounter, while transmission-based precautions add specific barriers for targeted routes of spread. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h7)

question: Which factor represents a common operational challenge in public health disease surveillance?

options.A: Underreporting by overburdened clinical personnel and poor diagnostic capacity
options.B: An excessive surplus of functional molecular testing laboratories in rural villages
options.C: Instantaneous electronic transmission of data from every household in the country
options.D: A complete absence of infectious diseases occurring within modern populations

explanation: Heavy workloads, lack of diagnostic tools, and administrative fatigue frequently lead to missed cases and delayed reporting. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h8)

question: Why is establishing feedback loops from central health authorities to frontline reporting nurses important?

options.A: It ensures that nurses receive financial bonuses for every patient admitted
options.B: It prevents regulatory bodies from inspecting clinical facilities
options.C: It maintains morale and encourages continued compliance with reporting protocols
options.D: It allows nurses to take over the ministerial duties of health directors

explanation: When frontline nurses see that their reported data leads to actionable public health interventions, they remain motivated to maintain rigorous reporting habits. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h8)
